new.title: Climb to Eğil Castle and the Assyrian rock tombs
new.desc: Eğil is the ancient Carcathiocerta, capital of the kingdom of Sophene, on the Tigris north-west of Diyarbakır. The castle stands on a rock outcrop cut free from the plateau, and rock-cut royal tombs line the nearby cliffs, with an Assyrian-style relief on the site.
new.tip: Go in the morning in spring or autumn; the tombs sit above the Dicle reservoir shore, so wear sturdy shoes. Eğil lies about 50 km from Diyarbakır by road.

new.title: Cross the Malabadi Bridge over the Batman River
new.desc: Built in the 12th century under the Artuqid ruler Timurtash, this single-arch stone bridge near Silvan has a main arch of about 40 m, long considered the longest of its type. It is on the UNESCO tentative list and still carries pedestrians beside a modern bridge.
new.tip: Come in the evening for soft light on the stone and the river below. Entry is free.

new.title: See the Artuqid Great Mosque of Silvan
new.desc: Silvan's Ulu Cami, in medieval Mayyafariqin, is a key Artuqid mosque. Its dome collapsed in 1152 and was rebuilt by 1157, and locals call it the Selahaddin Eyyubi Mosque after Ayyubid repairs. A rectangular plan with the dome before the mihrab links Central Asian and Anatolian Turkish mosque design.
new.tip: Visit outside prayer times and dress modestly. The old town castle and walls are a short walk away.

new.title: Tour the new Hasankeyf Museum and Archaeological Park
new.desc: The three-floor museum in New Hasankeyf shows finds from the Ilısu Dam rescue excavations and scale models of the old town. Beside it, the Archaeological Park holds the Artuqid and Ayyubid monuments moved before the reservoir filled, with an amphitheatre.
new.tip: Allow two hours for the museum plus the park. Check opening hours with the Batman museum directorate before travelling.
new.q: Hasankeyf Müzesi, Kültür Mahallesi, Müze Caddesi, Hasankeyf, Batman

new.title: Visit the relocated Zeynel Bey Tomb
new.desc: This round brick mausoleum, built in the 15th century for a son of the Aq Qoyunlu ruler Uzun Hasan, was moved in one piece in 2017 to the Hasankeyf cultural park, about 2 km from its original site. It has glazed turquoise tile bands and is the only Anatolian tomb of its type.
new.tip: Pair it with the museum and park next door. Late afternoon light brings out the tile colours.
new.q: Zeynel Bey Türbesi, Hasankeyf Kültür Parkı, Hasankeyf, Batman

new.title: Look over the Tigris from Hasankeyf Castle
new.desc: The citadel rises about 100 m above the Tigris and was not flooded when the Ilısu reservoir filled. Cave dwellings, the Artuqid middle gate and the minaret of the Er-Rızk mosque remain around the old town, now partly under water.
new.tip: Climb in the morning to avoid the heat and check that the castle is open on the day. A boat tour gives the reverse view.

new.title: Find 5,000-year-old gaming pieces at Batman Museum
new.desc: Opened in 2010, the museum shows Paleolithic to Artuqid finds from rescue digs in Batman and Siirt. Highlights are the Başur Höyük gaming stones from about 3000 BC and reliefs from Hasankeyf's old bridge, with an open-air park of reconstructed buildings.
new.tip: It is in the Cultural Center complex; check days and hours first, as sources differ.

new.title: Explore the Assyrian reliefs at Birkleyn Caves
new.desc: In the Korha mountain north-west of Lice, the Dibni stream runs through a long cave called the Tigris Tunnel. Assyrian kings, including Tiglath-Pileser I and Shalmaneser III, carved reliefs at its mouth, and excavations showed human use since the Late Neolithic.
new.tip: The track is rough and the site is remote, so go with a local guide or driver and ask about access in Lice first.

new.title: Walk the 12,000-year-old Çayönü Tepesi settlement
new.desc: Çayönü, about 7 km from Ergani, is a Pre-Pottery Neolithic settlement occupied roughly 8600-6800 BC. Excavated since the 1960s, it shows early farming, grill-plan buildings and finds linked with the Taş Tepeler sites. Excavations resumed in 2025 and the site is being prepared for visitors.
new.tip: Check access with Ergani district office, as digging can close parts of the mound. Combine with the Hilar caves and Makam mountain.

new.title: Climb to Kral Kızı Castle above Genç
new.desc: The ruins on the hill about 2 km from Genç town centre are tied to a legend of the Persian ruler Dara building a fortress for his daughter. Two tomb towers (kümbets) stand within the same village.
new.tip: Wear walking shoes and go in clear weather for views over the Genç valley.

new.title: Visit the 1,500-year-old Mor Aho Monastery in Gercüş
new.desc: This Syriac Orthodox monastery in Arıca village near Gercüş dates to the 6th century and was restored in 2018 before opening to tourism. It has fine stonework and draws Syriac Christian visitors and travellers from abroad.
new.tip: Reached by road from Batman via Gercüş; ask locally for the key holder before driving out.
new.q: Mor Aho Manastırı, Arıca, Gercüş, Batman

new.title: Admire the walnut minbar of Siirt Ulu Cami
new.desc: Siirt's Great Mosque, dated by tradition to 1129 under a Seljuk sultan, has a single minaret and a minbar carved from walnut wood. It was restored in 1965 and sits in the old centre.
new.tip: Visit outside prayer times; dress modestly.
new.q: Siirt Ulu Camii, Siirt Merkez, Siirt

new.title: See the clock tower on Hükümet Caddesi, Siirt
new.desc: The Siirt clock tower on Hükümet Caddesi is one of the city's symbols. A tower of 1905 was replaced by a reconstruction finished in 1975.
new.tip: Good for a short stop on a stroll through the old centre.
new.q: Siirt Saat Kulesi, Siirt Merkez, Siirt

new.title: Stand on the glass terrace of Tillo Castle
new.desc: The Ottoman-era Tillo Castle was opened to visitors in 2016 with a glass viewing terrace about 1,100 m above the Botan valley. It is open daily 09:00-17:00 per local reports, and free.
new.tip: Go in clear weather; the terrace is best in the morning light.

new.title: Photograph İnce Kaya (Kormas) Castle near Şirvan
new.desc: This Byzantine-era castle in İncekaya village, about 10 km from Şirvan, resembles a small château on its rock. It is one of Siirt's lesser-visited historic sites.
new.tip: Ask in Şirvan for current road conditions; the last stretch is a village road.
new.q: İncekaya Kalesi, İncekaya Köyü, Şirvan, Siirt

new.title: Step onto the Floating Islands of Solhan
new.desc: In Hazarşah village, a crater lake holds islands of aquatic plants with trees growing on them that drift with the wind. It is a protected natural monument at roughly 22,000 visitors a year, so rules apply and no sticks are allowed.
new.tip: Follow ranger signs, avoid sticks, and visit in late spring or summer.

new.title: Take a boat tour on the Hasankeyf reservoir
new.desc: Tours start from the museum port on the Ilısu reservoir, run about an hour and pass the castle, cliffs, coves and the pierced cave. The Hasankeyf Kale Tourism Cooperative runs eight boats and captains explain the town's history.
new.tip: Go in the morning on weekdays; summer weekends are crowded. Confirm prices at the pier.

new.title: Hike into Botan Valley National Park
new.desc: Declared a national park in 2019, Botan covers about 120,000 decares in Siirt Merkez, Tillo and Eruh. The Uluçay gorge (about 370 m deep) and caves make it popular for hiking, paragliding and rafting.
new.tip: Go in spring or early summer when the creek is full; confirm access and security with locals.

new.title: Soak in the Kös hot springs near Bingöl
new.desc: The Kös thermal centre lies on the Bingöl-Karlıova road about 18 km from Bingöl. The water is around 47 degrees C, with sodium, bicarbonate and sulphate.
new.tip: Take a towel and swimsuit; ask about separate hours for women and men.

new.title: Hike Makam (Zülküf) Mountain above Ergani
new.desc: The summit of Makam mountain holds Ergani's fortress, the shrine of the Prophet Zülküf and the ruins of the Virgin Mary Church over the Tigris. A Ministry walking route links it with Hilar caves and Çayönü.
new.tip: Start early; the minibus from Diyarbakır does not leave from the district bus station.
new.q: Zülküf Peygamber Makamı, Makam Dağı Mahallesi, Ergani, Diyarbakır

new.title: Eat grilled meats at Çömçe Et Lokantası in Batman
new.desc: Opened in 1986 on Diyarbakır Caddesi, Çömçe is one of Batman's long-running meat restaurants and tops local lists with a 4.9 rating from thousands of reviews.
new.tip: Ask for the day's grilled meat and local sides; lunch fills early.
new.q: Çömçe Lokantası, Diyarbakır Caddesi, Kültür, Batman

new.title: Try büryan and perde pilavı at Örnek Büryan Salonu
new.desc: This büryan hall in Batı neighbourhood, Siirt, sells the pit-roasted lamb that carries Siirt's geographical indication of 2003; the pastry-crusted perde pilavı is the traditional guest rice dish.
new.tip: Order early in the day; ask whether perde pilavı is cooked that day.
new.q: Örnek Büryan Salonu, 701. Sokak, Batı Mahallesi, Siirt Merkez, Siirt

new.title: Order Bingöl gömme and tutmaç at Yado Çeşmesi
new.desc: Yado Çeşmesi Et Lokantası on the Bingöl-Elazığ road is listed for local dishes such as gömme and tutmaç.
new.tip: Ask what is on the daily local menu; confirm opening hours by phone.
new.q: Yado Çeşmesi Et Lokantası, Bingöl-Elazığ Karayolu 8. km, Bingöl

new.title: Eat Bingöl kavurma at Soğukçeşme Kavurma 1965
new.desc: Soğukçeşme Kavurma, founded in 1965 and with several branches, is known for kavurma, the slow-fried meat dish of Bingöl.
new.tip: Eat it with bread and a salad at lunch.
new.q: Soğukçeşme Kavurma 1965, Çobantaşı, Bingöl Merkez, Bingöl
